title: Finite-height faithfully flat valuation extension to a separable closure
statement: Let $V$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], meaning $V\subseteq K$ and for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Let $K^s/K$ be a separable closure, meaning an algebraic separable extension whose field has no nontrivial finite separable extension [def-kun-separably-closed]. There exists a valuation ring $V^s\subseteq K^s$ with fraction field $K^s$, $V^s\cap K=V$, and maximal ideal contracting to the maximal ideal of $V$, such that $V^s$ has the same height as $V$ and $V\to V^s$ is faithfully flat. Here height is the number of strict inclusions in the prime-ideal chain, and faithfully flat means that tensoring modules with $V^s$ is exact and reflects zero modules. Consequently the singleton $\operatorname{Spec}V^s\to\operatorname{Spec}V$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

source.place: Valuation extension as in Temkin Section 2.1; Stacks Tag 0ASH (more-algebra-lemma-inequality-general) gives torsion value-group quotient for algebraic extensions and hence equal height; Tag 0539 (more-algebra-lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat) and Tag 00HR (algebra-lemma-local-flat-ff) give faithful flatness of the dominating inclusion. Existence also appears in lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension] to the embedding $K\hookrightarrow K^s$ and the valuation ring $V$. Its statement supplies a valuation ring $W\subseteq K^s$ with fraction field $K^s$ dominating $V$, hence with $\mathfrak m_W\cap V=\mathfrak m_V$. Moreover $W\cap K=V$, either directly from its combined conclusion or by [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection]. Set $V^s=W$. This uses the extension theorem for an arbitrary field extension, so no finiteness or perfection hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 00IA, algebra-lemma-dominate; intersection as in Tag 052K, algebra-lemma-x-or-x-inverse-valuation-ring.

proof.text: The extension $K^s/K$ is algebraic by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height] with $E=K^s$ and its valuation ring $W$. Its restriction is $W\cap K=V$ by step 1, so contraction is an order isomorphism on prime ideals. It sends strictly increasing chains bijectively to strictly increasing chains. Since the primes of $V$ form a finite chain, those of $W$ do also, with exactly the same number of strict inclusions. Thus $W$ has precisely the required finite height.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, more-algebra-lemma-inequality-general, finite-extension input to the algebraic-height lemma; the order-isomorphism consequence is the statement of lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height.

proof.text: View $W\subseteq K^s$ as a $V$-module by the inclusion from step 1. It is torsion free: if $0\ne a\in V$ and $w\in W$ satisfy $aw=0$, the same equation holds in the field $K^s$, where $a\ne0$, and multiplication by $a^{-1}$ gives $w=0$. By [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] applied to the valuation ring $V$ and module $W$, the inclusion $V\to W$ is flat.

The valuation rings $V,W$ are local rings, and the inclusion is local because it maps $\mathfrak m_V$ into $\mathfrak m_W$ by domination in step 1. It is flat by step 3. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] gives faithful flatness and surjectivity of $p:\operatorname{Spec}W\to\operatorname{Spec}V$. In particular tensoring is exact and detects zero modules, as required by the statement.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] to the flat inclusion $V\to W$ of step 3. This proves that its spectrum morphism $p$ is flat in the scheme-theoretic sense, not just flat on global sections.

source.place: Tag 01U5, morphisms-lemma-flat-characterize, (4) implies (1) on the singleton affine charts.

proof.text: Let $U$ be any affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}V$ and put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, so $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] the inclusion $U\to\operatorname{Spec}V$ corresponds to a ring map $\rho:V\to R$ and is $\operatorname{Spec}\rho$; this makes $R$ a $V$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] the open subscheme $p^{-1}U$, with its inclusion and $p|_{p^{-1}U}$, is a fibre product $\operatorname{Spec}W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}V}U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] this fibre product is $\operatorname{Spec}(W\otimes_VR)$; so $p^{-1}U$ is affine. Surjectivity in step 4 gives $p(p^{-1}U)=U$. Thus for each affine open $U$ one affine open of the source already maps onto it; for $U=\varnothing$ use the empty family. Together with flatness from step 5 this is exactly the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. This proves the singleton fpqc assertion.
